description: Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada publishes hourly weather inputs for the La Salle River watershed near Elie, Manitoba, covering 1990–2013. The series includes precipitation, temperature, wind speed, solar radiation and relative humidity assembled for the Red-Assiniboine hydrological modelling project. Values were estimated from nearby stations using gap filling and temporal disaggregation, including linear regression and a Bartlett-Lewis rainfall model. CSV data and English and French HTML data dictionaries are freely available under the Open Government Licence - Canada. They can drive watershed runoff, irrigation and flood simulations at an hourly step. The companion La Salle discharge and water-chemistry deposits provide response variables for model evaluation. These are processed forcing estimates, not a single uninterrupted instrument record. Gap filling and disaggregation can alter rainfall timing and extremes, which limits their use in event-scale infrastructure design without further checks.
